sanskrit: marudgaṇāḥ sadā sādhyā yasyā dantā nareśvara | huṅkāre caturo vedān vidyātsāṅgapadakramān || 105 || ṛṣayo romakūpeṣu hyasaṃkhyātāstapasvinaḥ | daṇḍahasto mahākāyaḥ kṛṣṇo mahiṣavāhanaḥ || 106 || yamaḥ pṛṣṭhasthito nityaṃ śubhāśubhaparīkṣakaḥ | catvāraḥ sāgarāḥ puṇyāḥ kṣīradhārāḥ staneṣu ca || 107 ||
english: Cows are full of all the Devas and all the Devas are identical with a cow. O king, Śakra dwells always on the tips of the horns; Skanda occupies the chest; Brahmā the head; the Bull-emblemed Lord is in the forehead; the deities Moon and Sun are the two eyes. Sarasvatī dwells in the tongue. All the Sādhyas and groups of Maruts are her teeth, O king. One should know that all the four Vedas with the Aṅgas and duly arranged words are in the Huṃkāra (bellowing of cow). Sages, the innumerable ascetics, dwell in the pores of the hairs. Yama stands at the back always scrutinizing the auspicious and the inauspicious. He has a huge body. He is armed with a big staff. He is dark-complexioned and has a buffalo for his vehicle. The four meritorious oceans are the flowing currents of milk from her udders. Cow should be honoured by a sensible person always, because Gaṅgā who originated from the feet of Viṣṇu and destroys sins merely by her sight is stationed in the flowing milk. O son of Pāṇḍu, the sacred and all-auspicious Lakṣmī is always present in cow-dung. Hence smearing with cow-dung should be done. Gandharvas, Apsarās and Nāgas are well-established at the tips of the hoofs. Know that cow is identical with all the Tīrthas that are present on the ocean-girt earth. Hence Gavya (milk product) is sacred.
